scientific_question: Does Muon polar normalization amplify the tiny forward-visible Pair-VQ functional-gradient error under an identical dense momentum history enough to explain the compact self-path drift?

factorial.finding: Either compact side moves self-training to the same worse basin; the defect is coupled and dynamic rather than two independent static capacity errors.

frozen_layout_oracle.finding: A same-byte neuron-major c_proj layout neither improves fixed CE nor held-out residual action, so static coordinate layout is not binding.

functional_gradient.finding: The teacher-forced one-step compact task gradient is almost identical to dense before the optimizer map.

optimizer_transition.finding: An older compact-momentum chart showed large post-polar error, but it confounded momentum transport with polar sensitivity and predates the selected lossless reserved-escape FP16 momentum.

theory.same_history_control: At each frozen dense-path probe, both branches start from the identical live dense Muon momentum buffer M_t. Only the held-out task gradient differs: g_dense versus g_center from the forward-visible compact center.
theory.nesterov_requests: M_next_dense = mu M_t + g_dense; R_dense = g_dense + mu M_next_dense. M_next_center and R_center use the same equations and same M_t with g_center.
theory.polar_test: Compare R_dense to R_center before normalization, then compare muon_update(R_dense) to muon_update(R_center) after the identical five-step Newton-Schulz polar map.
theory.attribution: Because momentum history, learning rate, weight decay, dense trajectory, batches, and compact representation are held fixed, excess post-polar error is attributable only to amplification of the compact functional-gradient perturbation by Muon normalization.
theory.decision_consequence: A pass authorizes one zero-update regularized-polar discriminator. It does not authorize training. A failure rejects polar amplification as primary and redirects theory to recurrent codec-neighbor path stability; it does not authorize a coefficient sweep.

frozen_protocol.training_parent: exact 124M QK-only dense-MLP synchronized replay, seed 1337, 238 updates, LR 0.0024, fixed data and schedule
frozen_protocol.momentum_history: identical live dense buffer for both polar variants

frozen_gate.primary_candidate_selection: The forward-visible center must retain the already sealed functional-gradient pass before polar attribution is interpreted.

state_and_compute_contract.candidate_persistent_state: none; nonintervening dense replay analysis only

decision_rule.oracle_pass: Seal MUON_POLAR_AMPLIFIES_CODEC_GRADIENT_ERROR and preregister one zero-update regularized-polar discriminator. Do not launch an LM endpoint.
decision_rule.oracle_fail: Seal MUON_POLAR_NOT_PRIMARY and reject compact-specific polar repair. Return to a recurrent codec-neighbor stability discriminator derived from the Mapping Loss stability term.
